## {#today .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.todaymeta}
A one-day course on methods, in four parts of 90 minutes, on the housing-audit case
:::

:::: {.todaybox}
::: {.nonincremental .fs-85}
1. Credibility and tools – science, its crisis, and the toolchain
2. The claim and its estimand – the paper, estimands and causal graphs
3. Reproduction and exploration – one of the five reanalyses reproduced, and the specification menu
4. Multiverse, replication and preregistration – the curve, the new audit, one preregistered analysis
:::
::::

::: {.todaytake .fs-85}
You leave with a reproduced result, an estimand statement and a causal graph of your own, a preregistered analysis, and your results on a live class multiverse
:::

::: {.todaymeta}
Work along in the browser lab, solo or in pairs, or in your IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.) if you have installed the workspace
:::

::: notes
Welcome – good to have you here. A full day, in four parts of ninety minutes, and today the methods are in the foreground. The first part sets up everything else: what we are doing when we do social science, why people say it is in crisis, and the software without which none of it happens. The second goes inside one published experiment, in which a thousand emails asked housing authorities in the United States how to apply for public housing, and asks what question its claim actually answers. In the third you reproduce one of the five independent reanalyses of that claim, whichever you choose, and then start varying the analysis yourself. The fourth part is the centre of the day: we read the curve of every justifiable analysis and the chart that the class builds, meet the new study that tested the claim again, and you settle on the one analysis that you would publish.
:::
